title: Ketogenic Dietary Intervention as a Potential Adjunctive Therapy for Inflammatory Rheumatic Diseases
summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis are chronic inflammatory diseases characterized by dysregulation of the immune system and may lead to progressive joint damage. Treatment typically includes disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, corticosteroids, and biologic therapies. However, the combination of multiple medications may increase the risk of adverse effects and negatively affect long-term treatment adherence. Therefore, additional therapeutic approaches are needed.

In recent years, increasing evidence has demonstrated that nutrition plays an important role in regulating the immune system and inflammatory processes. In particular, dietary patterns characterized by a high intake of carbohydrates have been associated with chronic inflammation and may contribute to both the development and disease activity of inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

A ketogenic diet is characterized by a marked reduction in carbohydrate intake. Previous studies have shown that ketogenic diets can reduce inflammatory processes and influence the function of specific immune cell populations. Of particular interest are regulatory T cells, which help limit inflammatory responses, and T helper 17 cells, which promote inflammation. Numerous studies have demonstrated that these cell populations play a key role in the development and maintenance of inflammatory rheumatic diseases. Previous work has shown that a ketogenic diet may positively influence the balance between these immune cell populations. However, the underlying biological mechanisms and the effects in patients with rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis remain insufficiently understood.

The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of a 14-day inpatient ketogenic dietary intervention on immune cells and metabolic processes in patients with rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis. Forty patients will receive a ketogenic diet in addition to their existing therapy. Blood samples and clinical parameters will be collected before and after the intervention to assess changes in immune function, disease activity, general health status, and quality of life.

interventions.name: 14-day ketogenic dietary intervention in addition to unchanged standard therapy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis who have been receiving stable, unchanged pharmacological treatment for at least six weeks. Blood samples are collected and clinical scores and questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis or psoriatic arthritis
Stable and unchanged pharmacological therapy for at least six weeks
Written informed consent provided by the participant
Exclusion criteria:
- Active malignant disease
- Current ketogenic or carbohydrate-restricted diet
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women
